signals.name: removal_level_shift_curvature
signals.measurement_meaning: Removal fraction times squared aligned level shift; measures how level displacement magnitude and removal jointly vary.
signals.limitation: This cubic interaction extends the quadratic baseline, but input displacement does not establish error sensitivity. Three tasks provide limited evidence for transferable curvature.
signals.falsifying_response: Adding this feature fails to reduce task-balanced held-out Y prediction error beyond uncertainty under the fixed predictor.

signals.name: removal_directional_level_curvature
signals.measurement_meaning: Signed counterpart of removal-weighted squared level displacement, allowing different curvature for opposite shift directions.
signals.limitation: The supplied directional Y differences vary across tasks. Neither a universal coefficient sign nor a causal effect is established; this feature may correlate strongly with the symmetric term.
signals.falsifying_response: On future held-out tasks, adding this feature to the baseline plus the symmetric term produces no incremental Y error reduction beyond uncertainty, or worsens prediction.

reasoning: The largest supplied quadratic prediction errors include removal actions, whose Y responses show substantial and task-dependent directional asymmetry. These two terms permit removal-dependent symmetric and directional curvature beyond existing quadratic terms without identifiers or fitted thresholds. Z measures target-versus-complement improvement and is not substituted for global Y. These are retrospective candidates; no augmented-model performance has been measured.
